discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 081007
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
607 AM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry conditions expected today with highs around 70 and low
  afternoon humidities.

- A few sprinkles are possible near Lake Michigan Friday evening.

- More widespread light rain is expected early Sunday,
  especially east of I-69, associated with the remnants of
  Isaias. No significant impacts are anticipated.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 250 AM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

Large surface high on the upwind/subsident side of deep eastern 
Canada trough will slide across our area today and ensure another 
pleasant weather day. Expect just some passing high clouds and highs 
around 70F. There are some nonzero fire wx concerns today. Forecast 
soundings show relatively deep mixing into a very dry airmass. 
Surface dewpoints likely crash into the upper 30s this afternoon 
yielding RH values around 30 percent. Surface gradient is not 
particularly strong but deep mixing may yield some gusts up to 20 
mph. These values are still safely below red flag criteria and ten 
hour fuel moistures are still above 10 percent but we often see a 
few field/combine fires across the area in these conditions during 
harvest time.

Surface high slides to the southeast tonight and return flow ramps 
up during the day Friday. Several solutions still show some light 
rain showers developing on the nose of the best LLJ/theta-e surge 
set to clip our far NW CWA Fri evening. Added some low chance PoP's 
to account for this but the low level moisture surge will be 
significantly impacted by antecedent dry conditions and any rain 
amounts will be very light. SW flow/WAA will push highs well into 
the 70s on Fri and to around 80F on Sat. Clouds increase late Sat 
but dry conditions will hold through the daytime hours.

Attention then turns to the remnants of Isaias still set to lift 
into the Ohio Valley Sat night into Sunday. While exact details 
regarding the track and subsequent rainfall amounts in our CWA still 
show some variability, there is increasing concensus that the 
heaviest rain will lift through central and eastern Ohio while our 
CWA only receives a glancing blow of light rain. The only area to 
watch for some brief moderate rain will be our far SE around 
Portland to Lima but even there not expecting enough to cause any 
impacts. The remnants of Isaias look to get quickly absorbed into 
the mean westerlies with the best tropical moisture plume riding 
along and east of the Appalachians. The main circulation weakens 
substantially by the time it reaches Ohio and even wind gusts look 
to remain below 30 mph. Will obviously continue to watch this period 
closely but overall little/no impacts anticipated for our CWA.

Rain exits late in the day Sunday but another cold front arrives 
with our next chance of rain Mon night. After one more day near 80F 
on Monday, highs drop back into the 60s for the middle of next week 
with lows well into the 40s.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 606 AM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

VFR conditions are expected at the terminals, with light west-
northwest flow becoming calm/variable tonight.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 080552

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1252 AM CDT Thu Oct 08 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. today or
   tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   A mid-level cyclonic flow pattern will be in place today from the
   upper Mississippi Valley into the Northeast, as west-northwesterly
   flow aloft remains over most of the remainder of the nation. At the
   surface, a moist airmass will be located along the Gulf Coast, where
   isolated to scattered thunderstorms will be possible, mainly from
   southeastern Louisiana eastward to Florida. Additional storms may
   develop in parts of the Desert Southwest and Four Corners region.
   Scattered storms will also be possible in Iowa and from northern New
   York into northern New England. No severe threat is expected today
   or tonight across the continental U.S.

   ..Broyles/Squitieri.. 10/08/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 080530

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1230 AM CDT Thu Oct 08 2026

   Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER EXTREME
   SOUTHERN ALABAMA...MOST OF THE FLORIDA PANHANDLE...AND EXTREME
   SOUTHWEST GEORGIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A risk for tornadoes will develop across the northeastern Gulf
   coastal areas late Friday into early Saturday ahead of Isaias.

   ...Northern Gulf Coast...
   The latest NHC forecast track brings Isaias into southern Alabama
   and the western Florida Panhandle Friday night and into early
   Saturday morning, which places the most favorable tornado risk to
   the east. While there is uncertainty regarding forward speed, the
   mid 70s F dewpoints and therefore favorable instability will at
   least move inland across the coastal counties of AL/FL Panhandle by
   12Z Saturday (the end of the Day 2 period). 

   Several CAMs are now resolving moderate to strong UH tracks,
   especially over the western FL Panhandle. Model forecast soundings,
   while somewhat variable in regard to the exact amount of
   instability, all appear sufficient to support supercells with
   tornado risk as shear and low-level ascent will both be favorable.
   Supercells may become evident on radar over the Gulf, with tornado
   threat increasing as cells move ashore and surface winds gain a
   southerly component. As such, tornado probabilities have been
   increased for Friday Night.

   ..Jewell.. 10/08/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 080730

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CDT Thu Oct 08 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE FLORIDA
   PANHANDLE ACROSS MUCH OF WESTERN GEORGIA AND EASTERN ALABAMA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A corridor of tornado risk may develop out of the Florida Panhandle
   and into parts of Georgia and eastern Alabama on Saturday.

   ...Southeastern States...
   As Isaias merges with the developing shortwave trough over the Lower
   MS Valley on Saturday, moderate to strong wind fields will develop
   over much of the Southeast. East of the surface low track, strong
   southerly low-level winds will aid northward movement of moisture
   and instability from the FL Panhandle northward across eastern AL
   and across much of GA and the eastern Carolinas.

   It is anticipated that severe storms may be ongoing within a
   north-south oriented band east of the low, roughly from the FL
   Panhandle into far eastern AL and southwest GA. Some of the early
   day cells near or south of the effective warm front may produce
   tornadoes as low-level shear will be very strong. This threat area
   should lift north during the day across AL and GA. It should be
   noted that depending on the exact surface low track and warm front
   position, the Slight Risk area may be adjusted in later outlooks.

   Overnight, the warm front will continue to lift north, with
   additional destabilization possible toward the southern
   Appalachians, and Carolinas. A low severe probability has been added
   for the night time scenario, which should see generally lesser (but
   still favorable) shear values and boundary layer instability.

   ...AZ...
   The remnants of Rachel are forecast to spread across the region late
   Saturday into Sunday. As this occurs, moisture and instability will
   increase, as well as deep layer shear as a shortwave trough moves
   toward the region. Given the nocturnal timing of destabilization,
   and substantial model differences, will defer possible severe
   probabilities to later outlooks. At this time, it appears isolated
   cells cannot be ruled out into Sunday morning, but severe potential
   will depend heavily on proper destabilization.

   ..Jewell.. 10/08/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
